title: The recipe registry reads its levels from the certification records, and every modifier has the rule that keeps it in a run
request: Fix both gaps the adding-capability guide found, then push.
spec: The registry printed every kind as experimental although binary and matching were certified in their records; resolve_for kept a detected modifier through a hand-written condition per name, so a new modifier would be detected and dropped without a word.
plan: Read each part's latest certification verdict; hold it only for the version it judged
Store the judged version in new records
One table of keep rules, and a test that every modifier has one

decisions.decision: A record's level holds only for the version it judged; a changed part is experimental again.
decisions.why: A kind's version is a fingerprint of its code: a certification earned by older code says nothing about the new one.

decisions.decision: Old records without a version are trusted and said so; nothing under results/ is edited.
decisions.why: The repository never edits results files; the next certify run writes the version.

decisions.decision: Product default is never read from a record.
decisions.why: Certification cannot grant it: it needs more than runs.

decisions.decision: A missing keep rule fails a test rather than defaulting to keep.
decisions.why: Defaulting to keep would claim a modifier the engine may not apply; a failing test makes the builder decide.

change: dclab_rnd/recipes.py (verdicts, level_of, modifier_parts, KEEP, the printout), dclab_rnd/certify.py (versions in new records), tests/test_recipes.py, docs/guides/ADDING_CAPABILITY.md.

findings.defect: The registry showed binary and matching as experimental.
findings.scenario: python -m dclab_rnd.recipes after CRT-002 and CRT-003 certified them.
findings.cause: part_of always set level experimental and never read the records.
findings.fix: level_of reads the latest record per part, gated on the judged version.

findings.defect: A new modifier would be detected and then dropped from the run's recipe.
findings.scenario: A sixth modifier added to PARTS without editing resolve_for.
findings.cause: The kept filter named the five modifiers by hand.
findings.fix: One KEEP table; a test fails until every modifier has its rule.

measurements.name: The registry printout
measurements.gate: certified kinds show certified, modifiers show their recorded level
measurements.result: binary and matching certified (version not recorded), the five modifiers experimental (CRT-001)
limits: old records kept no version: their level is trusted until the next certify run

outcome: The registry tells the truth about each part's level, and a new modifier cannot be silently dropped.
lessons: A list that must name every member by hand needs a test that compares it with the source of the members.
risks: resolve_for now reads the certification folder on every run: a few small files.
